summary.plain: The electron-positron collider of the Budker Institute in Novosibirsk, Siberia, that ran from the 1970s to 2000 at energies up to 1.4 GeV. Its detectors OLYA, ND, CMD-2 and SND measured how electron-positron collisions make hadrons, the basis of modern low-energy data. It was rebuilt as VEPP-2000.
summary.technical: VEPP-2M e⁺e⁻ collider at BINP: centre-of-mass energy range 0.36-1.4 GeV, operating for experiments from 1975 (some sources 1972/1974) to 2000; detectors ND (1982-87), CMD-1, CMD-2 (1992-2000) and SND (1995-2000); modernised into VEPP-2000 after 2000.
